main_text.p: dū respondet: Priori quòd Constantem scilicet Imperatoris Fratrem ad Bellum Constantio fratri inferendum sollicita-uerit,his verbis. [Non infanio ego, non mente[?] captus sū, ut vel cogitâsse unquā me tale quid suspiceris. Quapropter ne alijs quidem percontantibus respõdere velim, ne iterùm dū excusō me, illi qui audiunt animi pendeant,tuę autem pie-tati magna & clara voce respondeo, manúq; extensa, (quod didici ab Apostolo) Deum in meam ipsius animam testor, & ut scribitur in Lib. Reg. iusiurandū concipio, testis sit Dominus, & testis sit Christus eius, (sinas quę so me loqui) nunquā in malum tui mentionē feci, apud fratrē tuū Beatæ memoriæ Constantē, Pijssimū Augustum, neq; illū aduersus te irritaui, ut calūniantur isti; imò contra, si quando eū conuenirem) mentionem ipse faciebat de humanitate tua, quod etiā tū accidit, cum Thelasius veniebat Pitybio-nem, & nos commoraremur Aquilæ. Deus conscius est, quàm ego ibi tuæ pietatis meminerim, & quæ ego per id temporis loquutus fuerim, Deus tuæ aliquando menti reuelabit, ut cognoscas Syco-

page.notes: Uncertain: "mente" at the start of the line has a letter before it that is hard to read. The word "sū" is read as "sum" with a tilde over the u. The word "ut" before "cognoscas" carries a small superscript mark in the print, which I have read as a printing mark and not as a letter. "quęso" is read as "quę so" with a space; the letters are probable, not certain, so the spacing may differ. Nothing else is doubtful. No page number, running head, catchword or signature is printed on this part.
